cases.prTitle: Check available stock before calculating allocation
cases.prDescription: Move the availability check ahead of the stock subtraction and keep allocation updates together.

expectedFindings.trigger: A positive requested quantity exactly equals the remaining stock
expectedFindings.rootCause: The >= comparison rejects an allocation that leaves zero units
expectedFindings.consequence: A customer cannot purchase all remaining units, including the last single unit
expectedFindings.evidence: Reserving eight notebooks from a stock of eight throws OUT_OF_STOCK at the branch head; base and the > correction succeed

expectedTestFailures: inventory supports complete allocation and replenishment

cases.prDescription: Read the reservation window from RESERVATION_TTL_SECONDS, validate its range, and document the configuration option.

expectedFindings.trigger: A reservation is created with the default or a valid configured lifetime
expectedFindings.rootCause: Configuration returns seconds while the reservation service adds that value directly to a millisecond timestamp
expectedFindings.consequence: Default reservations expire in 900 milliseconds rather than 15 minutes; checkout after two seconds fails and allocated stock is released prematurely
expectedFindings.evidence: Default expiry is 10900 instead of 910000 for a clock starting at 10000. Configured 120 seconds yields 10120 instead of 130000. Multiplying the returned value by 1000 restores both contracts

requiredContext.reason: Establishes the millisecond clock, the unconverted lifetime addition, and the stock-release consequence

expectedTestFailures: reservations support checkout during their advertised lifetime
reservation availability follows the expiration instant

cases.prDescription: Use an array reduction to calculate the merchandise subtotal while retaining the existing shipping calculation and order response.
cases.safeRationale: For the dense arrays of integer-priced order lines produced by shop.checkout, both versions visit lines in order and add the same products starting at zero. The explicit initial value also preserves empty-array behavior. Shipping and response construction are unchanged; the calculation does not mutate inputs.
cases.scope: Behavioral correctness of this refactor for application-produced lines; arbitrary sparse arrays, hostile objects and pre-existing missing product features are outside the contract
